title: Mirror Inversion

story.briefing: The lattice was installed back to front. Every junction has its two branches the wrong way round, all the way down.
story.success: Lattice mirrored. The branches finally match the schematic.

description: Return the mirror image of a binary tree: at every node the left and right subtrees are swapped, all the way down. Return it in the same array format, sized so that the last entry is not null (or empty, for an empty tree). A tree is given as an array where the node at index i has its left child at index 2i+1 and its right child at index 2i+2. A null entry means there is no node there, and nothing exists beneath it. An empty array is an empty tree.

examples.explanation: The right child moves left, and the trailing null is dropped.

hints: Swapping only the root children is not enough — every node in the tree needs the same treatment.
Because a node position in the output depends on the swaps made above it, it is easier to build a fresh array than to rearrange the original in place.

Walk the original from index 0. For a node at index i in the source, write its value at index j in the result, then recurse sending the source left child to the result right position and vice versa. Trim trailing nulls at the end.
